questions.question: A patient with classic hyperglycemic symptoms has random plasma glucose of 228 mg/dL. Which principle applies?
choices: Diabetes is excluded because no A1C is available
Random plasma glucose at least 200 mg/dL with classic symptoms meets an ADA diagnostic criterion
Only urine glucose can diagnose diabetes
The result must always be ignored during symptoms
questions.explanation: ADA criteria include random plasma glucose at least 200 mg/dL with classic hyperglycemic symptoms or crisis. Other asymptomatic results generally require confirmation.

questions.question: Why can serum potassium be normal or high when total-body potassium is depleted in DKA?
choices: The kidneys stop all potassium loss
Insulin deficiency and acidosis shift potassium out of cells while osmotic diuresis causes total-body loss
DKA creates potassium from glucose
Serum and total-body potassium are always identical
questions.explanation: Extracellular shifting can mask substantial urinary potassium loss, so potassium can fall rapidly during treatment and requires close monitoring.

questions.question: A patient with type 1 diabetes is ill and not eating. Which general sick-day principle is safest?
choices: Automatically stop basal insulin
Continue basal insulin under an individualized sick-day plan and monitor glucose, ketones, hydration, and warning signs
Avoid checking ketones
Wait for coma before seeking help
questions.explanation: Stopping basal insulin can precipitate DKA. Sick-day plans address insulin adjustment, glucose and ketone checks, hydration, and escalation.

questions.question: Which thyroid pattern most strongly suggests primary hypothyroidism?
choices: High TSH with low free T4
Low TSH with high free T4
Low free T4 with an inappropriately low TSH from pituitary disease
Normal TSH with severe hypercalcemia
questions.explanation: Primary thyroid failure lowers free T4 and removes negative feedback, leading to an elevated TSH.

questions.question: A patient who abruptly stopped long-term glucocorticoids has vomiting, hypotension, hyponatremia, and confusion. What is the priority?
choices: Wait several days for outpatient stimulation testing
Suspect adrenal crisis and provide immediate emergency glucocorticoid, fluids, and transfer
Start thyroid hormone only
Treat with an oral diuretic
questions.explanation: Severe adrenal insufficiency or crisis requires immediate treatment; diagnostic samples may be obtained only if they do not delay emergency care.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects KDIGO classification of CKD?
choices: One abnormal creatinine during dehydration proves CKD
CKD requires abnormalities for at least three months and is classified by cause, GFR, and albuminuria
Albuminuria never affects risk
G1 eGFR alone always means CKD
questions.explanation: CKD requires chronic kidney structure or function abnormality and is stratified with cause, GFR category, and albuminuria category.

questions.question: A patient has fever, flank pain, pyuria, and hydronephrosis behind an obstructing stone. What is the best management principle?
choices: Oral antibiotics alone are always sufficient
This is an infected obstruction requiring urgent antibiotics, decompression, and hospital-level care
Wait for spontaneous passage regardless of sepsis risk
Use only a diuretic
questions.explanation: Infection behind obstruction is a source-control emergency and requires urgent drainage plus antimicrobial and supportive management.

questions.question: Which finding pattern most suggests nephritic disease?
choices: Hematuria with casts, hypertension, and declining kidney function
Isolated allergic rhinitis
Normal urinalysis with ankle trauma
Hyperglycemia without urine abnormalities
questions.explanation: A nephritic pattern includes glomerular hematuria, casts, hypertension, and impaired kidney function and may require expedited nephrology evaluation.

questions.question: A patient has severe symptomatic hyponatremia. Why must correction be carefully controlled?
choices: Sodium has no effect on the brain
Overly rapid correction can cause serious neurologic injury
The exact rate never matters
All hyponatremia should be corrected at home
questions.explanation: Both severe hyponatremia and overly rapid correction can injure the brain, so symptomatic cases require monitored emergency management.

questions.question: An older adult with CKD, cognitive impairment, and recurrent hypoglycemia has a very low A1C. What is the best next step?
choices: Intensify insulin automatically
Review glucose patterns and deintensify high-hypoglycemia-risk therapy when appropriate to individualized goals
Ignore the episodes
Set the same target for every adult
questions.explanation: Recurrent hypoglycemia is dangerous. Treatment and targets should be individualized for kidney function, cognition, frailty, burden, and patient goals.
